llm_role: LLM-based/agent-based root-cause diagnosis; artifact-specialized agents reason over source-level semantics and kernel configurations and build Evidence Graphs.
security_task: unknown (kernel crash root-cause diagnosis; security relevance not stated)
evidence: we propose KernelDiag, an agent-based framework for kernel root-cause diagnosis via structured causal reasoning.
uncertainty: Security relevance is not stated; crash diagnosis may be reliability-focused.

os_target: kernel and compiler code in C and Rust
llm_role: LLM agents infer specifications, select checks, classify counterexamples, and propose refinements; a bounded model checking backend verifies.
security_task: unknown (verification of safety contracts and panic-freeness; security vulnerability task not stated)
evidence: We instantiate the approach in BMC-Agent and evaluate it on LLM-generated kernel and compiler code in C and Rust alongside mature OSS-Fuzz-hardened libraries, confirming real defects, producing bounded clean verifications on heavily-fuzzed surfaces, and establishing functional equivalence on selected algorithmic functions.
uncertainty: Safety and functional correctness are explicit, but security is not.

llm_role: Claude Code coding agents with four underlying LLMs use security skills to audit code; SKILL-SIF evolves skills from failure patterns.
security_task: vulnerability detection at function, statement, and vulnerability-class levels
evidence: We conduct the first large-scale empirical study of 37 security skills using Claude Code with four underlying LLMs on 100 real Linux kernel vulnerabilities across ten classes, totaling 14800 runs.
uncertainty: All three dimensions are explicit; the work is an evaluation/framework study rather than a deployed OS defense.

llm_role: DUALLM combines an LLM and a fine-tuned small language model to classify patches using titles/messages, diffs, and code context.
security_task: identify security-critical patches addressing out-of-bounds and use-after-free vulnerabilities
evidence: by leveraging cues from commit titles/messages and diffs alongside appropriate code context, we develop DUALLM, a dual-method pipeline that integrates two approaches based on a Large Language Model (LLM) and a fine-tuned small language model.
uncertainty: OS target and security task are explicit; the LLM is one of two classifiers.

llm_role: K-Repro is an LLM-based agentic system with controlled code browsing, VM management, interaction, and debugging that generates PoCs.
security_task: N-day vulnerability reproduction
evidence: we develop K-Repro, an LLM-based agentic system equipped with controlled code-browsing, virtual machine management, interaction, and debugging capabilities.
uncertainty: All three dimensions are explicit; reproduction success is partial.

os_target: Linux kernel (one of three domains; also userspace programs and Google V8)
llm_role: AI agents progressively extend a vulnerability-triggering input into a working exploit.
security_task: vulnerability exploitation
evidence: Given a program input that triggers a vulnerability, ExploitGym tasks agents with progressively extending it into a working exploit.
uncertainty: Linux kernel is one of three domains; this is a capability benchmark, not a deployed OS tool.

llm_role: LLMs are evaluated for vulnerability detection and patch generation; the framework assesses their outputs.
security_task: software vulnerability detection and patching
evidence: This paper introduces VulnLLMEval, a framework designed to assess the performance of LLMs in identifying and patching vulnerabilities in C code.
uncertainty: The kernel is the dataset source; the framework evaluates LLMs rather than integrating them into an OS.

os_target: kernel enforcement boundary with pre-installed eBPF map updates
llm_role: LLM-assisted planners/agents translate observations into typed security intents, which a deterministic governor admits or rejects.
security_task: adaptive security enforcement and admission control against three threat classes
evidence: We propose a split-control architecture in which an untrusted planner emits typed security intents, a deterministic governor checks each intent against safety, resource, temporal-stability, and proportionality invariants, and only admitted actions are bound to signed receipts and compiled into pre-installed eBPF map updates.
uncertainty: LLM-assisted planners are one planner class; the governor, not the LLM, is the core security mechanism.

llm_role: Eight vanilla LLMs and 15 LoRA fine-tuned variants perform non-targeted and targeted vulnerability detection and CWE classification.
security_task: vulnerability detection and CWE classification
evidence: We present CWE-Trace, a framework for LLM vulnerability detection built from 834 manually curated Linux kernel samples spanning 74 CWEs.
uncertainty: All three dimensions are explicit; the focus is diagnostic evaluation, not an OS-integrated detector.

llm_role: Vul-RAG augments LLMs with multi-dimensional vulnerability knowledge via retrieval-augmented generation for detection.
security_task: vulnerability detection and identifying previously unknown bugs
evidence: We design a novel knowledge-level Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework Vul-RAG, which improves LLMs with an accuracy increase of 16% - 24% in identifying vulnerable and patched code.
uncertainty: The kernel is the evaluation and detection target; deployment inside the OS is not described.

os_target: COTS Windows binaries and Windows kernel targets/kernel drivers
llm_role: SLYP is a ReAct-style LLM-agent pipeline with MCP servers for binary exploration and dynamic debugging; it synthesizes debugger-verified PoCs.
security_task: end-to-end vulnerability discovery and validation
evidence: we build SLYP, a REACT-style pipeline for end-to-end vulnerability discovery and validation of COTS binaries.
uncertainty: Windows kernel is an additional target; the main benchmark is COM binaries.

os_target: Linux kernel (one of three targets; also V8 and SpiderMonkey)
llm_role: Frontier models and coding agents hunt vulnerabilities and produce working PoC inputs; an LLM-based judge grades them.
security_task: long-horizon vulnerability discovery and PoC reproduction
evidence: We present SEC-bench Pro, a benchmark that measures how well frontier models hunt real vulnerabilities by reproducing working PoC inputs from disclosed reports, where each task pairs a concrete bug with the instructions for triggering it.
uncertainty: Linux kernel is one of three targets; this is a benchmark study.

os_target: container filesystem isolation and privileged host-container interactions
llm_role: Grounded semantic patterns guide LLM reasoning to detect container-escape logic flaws; the framework also generates and verifies patches.
security_task: container escape vulnerability detection and remediation
evidence: Grounded patterns guide LLM reasoning, while isolated Proof-of-Concept (PoC) execution validates findings.
uncertainty: The analyzed code is container components; kernel defenses are discussed as context.

os_target: unknown (Linux kernel appears only in the CVE corpus; target code is not established as an OS component)
llm_role: AutoPatch is a multi-agent framework using RAG, semantic/taint analysis, and enhanced chain-of-thought to verify and patch vulnerable LLM-generated code.
security_task: patching real-world CVE vulnerabilities
evidence: we propose AutoPatch, a multi-agent framework designed to patch vulnerable LLM-generated code, particularly those introduced after the LLMs' knowledge cutoff.
uncertainty: Security task and LLM role are clear, but no OS component is established as the patching target.

os_target: Docker/OCI container sandboxes (kernel flaws are one escape mechanism)
llm_role: LLMs act as adversarial agents with shell access attempting to escape a container sandbox.
security_task: container sandbox escape
evidence: Following a threat model of a motivated adversarial agent with shell access inside a container, SANDBOXESCAPEBENCH covers a spectrum of sandboxescape mechanisms spanning misconfiguration, privilege allocation mistakes, kernel flaws, and runtime/orchestration weaknesses.
uncertainty: The benchmark evaluates LLM capability; kernel/OS is one escape surface rather than the sole target.

llm_role: An LLM and differential-model framework extracts protocol specifications and performs incremental code-function analysis across kernel versions.
security_task: detect RFC-implementation inconsistencies and potential vulnerabilities
evidence: By modeling the iterative relationship of the protocol and based on the iterative update relationship of the RFC standard, we perform incremental code function analysis on different versions of kernel code implementations to automatically perform code detection and vulnerability analysis.
uncertainty: The OS target is kernel protocol-stack code; the specific kernel and LLM architecture are not named.

llm_role: BugLens guides LLMs through structured reasoning to assess security impact and validate constraints from source code.
security_task: vulnerability/bug detection and false-positive reduction
evidence: BugLens guides LLMs through structured reasoning steps to assess security impact and validate constraints from the source code.
uncertainty: All three dimensions are explicit; the LLM is a post-refinement layer atop static analysis.

os_target: eBPF kernel extension mechanism (Linux, ported to Windows)
llm_role: The LLM synthesizes eBPF programs from English prompts, with LLM-empowered program comprehension, symbolic execution, and feedback loops.
security_task: unknown (functional kernel extension synthesis; security is mentioned only as general motivation)
evidence: KEN uses recent advances in large language models (LLMs) to synthesize an eBPF program given a user's English language prompt.
uncertainty: The abstract describes functional extension authoring and verifier compatibility, not a security detection or enforcement task.

llm_role: An LLM editor refines static-analysis checkers using analyzer evidence, source context, and validation feedback.
security_task: vulnerability checker refinement and kernel bug detection
evidence: SemWeaver is a plug-in refinement layer that extracts patch-relevant analyzer evidence and assembles it with source context and validation feedback into a structured, provenance-labelled bundle.
uncertainty: The LLM role is checker editing; the OS target is Linux kernel fixes and checkers.

llm_role: The LLM translates historical patches into typestate rules; a shared backend executes those rules for bug detection.
security_task: kernel bug detection from patch-derived typestate rules
evidence: An LLM translates each patch into a typestate rule specifying its tracked object, actions, guards, transitions, and violations.
uncertainty: All three dimensions are explicit; the LLM does not itself perform program analysis, which is delegated to the backend.
